title: Cloud platform selection
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Let's dive into the cloud strategy discussion. I've been looking at various options, and I'd like to share my thoughts.

SRE: Before we go any further, I want to talk about the complexity of managing a hybrid solution. I'm worried it might become a headache.

CTO: I understand your concerns, John. But let's not jump the gun. Let's first discuss the pros and cons of the options at hand.

Finance Partner: Alright, so we've got AWS Sole-Source Strategy, Google Cloud Platform Exclusive, and Microsoft Azure Exclusive on the table, correct?

Platform Engineering Lead: That's right. We've considered the costs, features, and support services for each.

SRE: I've looked into the details, and I must say, the Google Cloud Platform Exclusive option seems too costly for the benefits we'd realistically gain.

CTO: Agreed. I've also had reservations about the high costs associated with that option. Let's not pursue it further.

Platform Engineering Lead: Similarly, the Microsoft Azure Exclusive doesn't seem to offer the best support services for our specific use cases.

CTO: Well put, Alex. So, it looks like we're left with the AWS Sole-Source Strategy. But I'd like to hear more about why you recommend a hybrid approach, Alex.

Platform Engineering Lead: AWS offers the most feature-rich suite for our needs, while Google Cloud offers competitive pricing for specific services. By adopting a hybrid strategy, we can minimize costs while leveraging the strengths of both platforms.

SRE: I see the logic in that, but still, managing two cloud providers will add complexity to our work.

CTO: I understand your concerns, John. But let's take it one step at a time. We can work out the details and devise a migration plan that focuses on minimizing service disruptions during the transition.

Finance Partner: Alright, let's give it a shot. I'll work with the finance team to ensure we have the budget for this.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'll take ownership of the project and work with the teams to devise the migration plan and manage the hybrid solution.

CTO: Sounds good. I'll sign off on this decision. We're moving forward with a hybrid cloud solution consisting of AWS and Google Cloud Platform for our infrastructure needs.

SRE: Alright, but just remember, I'll be here to voice my concerns if things get too complicated.

CTO: Absolutely, John. We appreciate your input. Now, let's take a quick break before diving into the next topic.

Assistant: Coffee anyone? (Off-topic exchange)

CTO: Sure, that sounds great, Alex. Let's grab a coffee before we continue.

Platform Engineering Lead: Sounds like a plan, CTO. I'll join you in a moment.

Assistant: I'll get the coffees ready then. (End of off-topic exchange)

Title: Decision on Hybrid Cloud Strategy Adoption

Following the meeting, it was decided to adopt a hybrid cloud solution incorporating AWS and Google Cloud Platform for infrastructure needs. This strategy was chosen to optimize costs while capitalizing on the strengths of both platforms.

The Sole-Source Strategy with AWS was deemed non-optimal due to subpar support services for our specific use cases. Microsoft Azure was excluded from the selected platforms due to insufficient support.

The SRE raised concerns about the complexity of managing a hybrid solution. A detailed migration plan, aimed at minimizing service disruptions during the transition, will be developed in due course.
